title: Influence formula for a unate coordinate
statement: Let $n\ge0$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be $\pm1$-valued, and let $i\in[n]$. Suppose its discrete derivative $D_i f(x)=\tfrac12(f(x_{i\leftarrow0})-f(x_{i\leftarrow1}))$ is nonnegative at every point, or is nonpositive at every point. Then the influence of coordinate $i$ equals the absolute value of the Fourier--Walsh coefficient at the singleton frequency: $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]=|\widehat f(\{i\})|$.
hypotheses_covered: The discrete derivative in coordinate $i$ is everywhere nonnegative or everywhere nonpositive
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. Put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ and real cube functions $h$. For a real cube function $h$, write $D_i h(x)=\tfrac12(h(x_{i\leftarrow0})-h(x_{i\leftarrow1}))$, where $x_{i\leftarrow b}$ replaces bit $i$ by $b$. Set $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E[(h(x)-h(x^{\{i\}}))^2]$ and $I(h)=\sum_i I_i(h)$, where $x^{\{i\}}$ flips bit $i$. If $h$ is sign-valued and either $D_i h(x)\ge0$ for all $x$ or $D_i h(x)\le0$ for all $x$, then $I_i(h)=|\widehat h(\{i\})|$.
